title: Even and Odd Function Decomposition of a Rational Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Decompose the rational function f(x) = \frac{x+2}{x+1} into the unique sum of an even function f_E(x) and an odd function f_O(x) on its symmetric domain of validity \mathbb{R} \setminus \{-1, 1\}.
hints: Recall the fundamental decomposition formulas: f_E(x) = [f(x) + f(-x)] / 2 and f_O(x) = [f(x) - f(-x)] / 2.
Carefully compute f(-x) by replacing x with -x and rewriting with a positive leading coefficient in the denominator.
Find a common denominator for f(x) + f(-x) and f(x) - f(-x), then divide by 2.

steps.title: State the Even-Odd Decomposition Formulas
steps.mathExpression: f(x) = f_E(x) + f_O(x) \quad \text{where} \quad f_E(x) = \frac{f(x) + f(-x)}{2}, \quad f_O(x) = \frac{f(x) - f(-x)}{2}
steps.explanation: Any real function defined on a domain symmetric about 0 can be written uniquely as the sum of an even component and an odd component.
steps.why: The sum f_E + f_O identically yields f(x), while f_E(-x) = f_E(x) and f_O(-x) = -f_O(x).

steps.title: Evaluate f(-x) and Standardize Form
steps.explanation: Replacing x with -x yields (-x + 2)/(-x + 1). Factoring -1 from numerator and denominator simplifies the expression to (x - 2)/(x - 1), defined for x != 1.
steps.why: Standardizing denominators simplifies combining algebraic fractions with common denominators.

steps.title: Compute the Even Component f_E(x)
steps.explanation: Expanding the numerators gives (x+2)(x-1) = x^2 + x - 2 and (x-2)(x+1) = x^2 - x - 2. Adding them eliminates the linear terms, leaving (2x^2 - 4)/(x^2 - 1). Multiplying by 1/2 gives (x^2 - 2)/(x^2 - 1).
steps.why: Adding a function to its reflection eliminates all odd powers, leaving a purely even function.

steps.title: Compute the Odd Component f_O(x)
steps.explanation: Subtracting the numerators cancels the quadratic and constant terms: (x^2 + x - 2) - (x^2 - x - 2) = 2x. Multiplying by 1/2 leaves x/(x^2 - 1).
steps.why: Subtracting a reflected function cancels all even powers, leaving a purely odd function.

steps.title: Verify Parity and Sum
steps.explanation: Checking: f_E(-x) = ((-x)^2 - 2)/((-x)^2 - 1) = (x^2 - 2)/(x^2 - 1) (even), and f_O(-x) = (-x)/((-x)^2 - 1) = -x/(x^2 - 1) (odd). Their sum recombines directly to f(x).
steps.why: Verifying both algebraic parities and reconstituting the original function proves the uniqueness of the decomposition.
